text:
matt_cust: hey — hitting an embeddings error when batching from our client. we used the new embeddings endpoint and suddenly getting dimension mismatch errors. works for single tests but fails in prod when we batch. stack trace attached below. :(
sarah_support: sorry you're blocked — can you paste the exact request body you send? and the API error you get?
matt_cust: here's the failing curl we use (we're node client → server → curl to redwood):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-XXXX' \  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \  -d '{"model":"embed-large","input":"[\"doc1\", \"doc2\"]"}'
```
error returned: 400 Bad Request {"error":"Invalid input shape: expected 2D array of strings (batch), got string. dimension check failed"}

sarah_support: ah — I think the body has a double-encoded JSON string for `input`. you sent input as a single string that contains a JSON array. the embeddings API expects `input` to be an array (or a single primitive) — but when you send a JSON-encoded string the server interprets it as a single item with wrong shape. can you show the code that builds the body?
matt_cust: gist of our node helper that builds the payload:
```js
// in our server
const payload = JSON.stringify({model: 'embed-large', input: JSON.stringify(items)});
await fetch(EMBED_URL, {method: 'POST', headers: {'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'Authorization': `Bearer ${KEY}`}, body: payload});
```
so yeah we stringify twice because we pass items around as strings in earlier pipe.
devon_sdk: that explains it. common bug: double-stringifying or passing a scalar vs array. the correct body should be: 
```json
{"model":"embed-large","input":["doc1","doc2"]}
```
or if sending a single doc: 
```json
{"model":"embed-large","input":"single doc text"}
```
server-side libs should not wrap the array in a string.

oliver_eng: also note some users accidentally send nested arrays (e.g., `[["doc1"],["doc2"]]`) from fancy batching helpers; that produces shape [N,1] and then later our internal dimension checks throw something like: `Dimension mismatch: expected dims=1536 but got dims=[1]` when the model returns vector shapes. double-check that `input` is a flat array of strings or a single string.
matt_cust: thanks — we fixed the immediate issue. curious: our logs showed a different error message earlier: `Invalid embedding vector length (1536 expected, 1536x1 received)`. is that the same root cause?
sarah_support: yes — that's downstream. because the request got parsed as an array of arrays or as tokens, our runtime treated each inner element as a vector and attempted to validate the returned array shape. it results in confusing wording. I'll file a docs + server-better-error ticket to make the message clearer.

matt_cust: for posterity, here's the correct minimal repro (curl + python + js) we tested locally that fixed it:
1) curl (correct):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-XXXX' \  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \  -d '{"model":"embed-large","input":["first doc","second doc"]}'
```
2) node (fetch):
```js
const body = {model: 'embed-large', input: items}; // items is an array of strings\await fetch(url, {method: 'POST', headers: {'Content-Type':'application/json', Authorization: `Bearer ${KEY}`}, body: JSON.stringify(body)});
```
3) python (requests):
```py
import requests
body = {"model": "embed-large", "input": ["a","b"]}
requests.post(url, headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {KEY}"}, json=body)
```

devon_sdk: extra checklist for SDKs & clients: make sure your SDKs accept both `input: str` and `input: list[str]` and do NOT auto-wrap a list into a JSON string. also validate `Content-Type: application/json` — some frameworks pass `text/plain` or forget `json=` vs `data=` in python which leads to similar double-encoding.

oliver_eng: performance note — batching many small docs is fine, but avoid nesting arrays expecting auto-flattening. our runtime expects a single-level batch; nested batches will degrade throughput and sometimes trigger unexpected dimension checks in the CPU/GPU path. keep the client-side shapes flat so server can do continuous batching efficiently.

matt_cust: one more oddity: we saw intermittent failures when we used our queueing layer (it stores `items` as a string in DB). sometimes requeued payloads arrived double-encoded. we now changed the queue to store JSON arrays natively.
sarah_support: good call. I'll add a short troubleshooting snippet to the support KB with the common causes: double-stringify, nested arrays, wrong content-type, sending token arrays instead of raw text.

ingest-bot: notice: created ticket INF-2273 to update runtime error strings and add a KB entry.

matt_cust: thanks all — unblocked. appreciate the quick triage :thumbsup:

sarah_support: any follow-ups, ping me. if you want we can schedule a quick review of your queuing layer and client helper functions to make sure no other endpoints will get similar issues.
matt_cust: maybe later — for now shipping fix. cheers!
